## Sophia modules (sophia.html) · 5 passages

- **ap**: … It played a documented role in advancing the 21st Century Peace Through Strength Act, which provided $14.3 billion in emergency military aid to Israel. Speaker Mike Johnson has ties to both AIPAC and CUFI — embodying the dual enforcement mechanism in one of the most powerful legislative positions in the country.
- **ap**: … In the 2024 election cycle, 318 AIPAC-endorsed candidates won congressional seats. This is not 318 identical candidates — they span a wide ideological range, from progressive Democrats to far-right Republicans, from Ted Lieu to Mike Johnson. What they share is AIPAC's endorsement and the expectation of alignment on Israel-related legislation.
- **ap**: … The direct tier of AIPAC's network consists of 318 endorsed and elected members of Congress in the 2024 cycle — a supermajority of the 435-member House. These members span a wide ideological range: from Ted Lieu and Pete Aguilar on the Democratic left to Mike Johnson and Tom Emmer on the Republican right. What they share is AIPAC endorsement, documented contribution histories, and — in the case of the majority — participation in AIPAC-funded orientation trips to Israel.
- **ap**: … Much of current-day support for Israeli policy within the Republican Party and its voter base can be traced to CUFI's organizational reach. Speaker Mike Johnson has ties to both AIPAC and CUFI — embodying the dual enforcement mechanism at the highest level of House leadership. CUFI played a documented role in advancing the 21st Century Peace Through Strength Act, which provided $14.3 billion in emergency military aid to Israel, by mobilizing its member network for congressional contact campaigns.
- **legislativearch**: During the 2025-2026 shutdown, reporting found the White House's Office of Management and Budget removed language from its own guidance affirming the 2019 law's back-pay guarantee for furloughed employees specifically (as opposed to those required to work without pay), prompting a bipartisan letter from Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and several Democratic colleagues urging OMB to follow the law as written. [cite:shutdown_pay_asymmetry] Speaker Mike Johnson said he had not discussed the matter with the White House but hoped furloughed workers would receive back pay; Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he was "not familiar" with the 2019 law. This is presented as a live, actively disputed situation rather than a settled fact, consistent with this module's currency-discipline standard for ongoing controversies.
